lead: Shops, a market and long-standing neighbours, between Plaça d'Espanya and Sants station.
text: Its name comes from the inn that Joan Corrades i Bosch built in the mid-19th century and named after his home village, Hostafrancs del Sió. Around it grew a working-class and commercial neighbourhood that today lives off Carrer de la Creu Coberta, one of the busiest streets in Barcelona, and its market, designed by Antoni Rovira i Trias and opened in 1888. Until 1839 it was part of the municipality of Santa Maria de Sants; the market and the Vinyeta slaughterhouse, from 1891, boosted its trade, and by the early 20th century it already had 16,474 inhabitants, counting the Creu Coberta and Àngel districts.

Since the 1980s, middle-class professionals and families have settled here, giving the neighbourhood a more varied profile without losing its close-knit feel. Every year it celebrates its festa major in honour of Sant Àngel Custodi, with the bouquet dance and the devils' dance. If you are selling, the average sale price (4,041 €/m² in 2025) is 4% above the Sants-Montjuïc average. Within the neighbourhood, the price of each flat depends on its condition, its floor and its building, so it is best to compare it with nearby sales rather than with the district average. If you are buying, an 80 m² flat costs about 323,000 € on average, and this is one of the most expensive neighbourhoods in Sants-Montjuïc (2nd of 8 by price). If you are investing, the average rent (960 €/month) is 4% below the district; before deciding, it is worth studying each deal with real figures for purchase, renovation and rental income.
housing: Buildings from the early 20th century, on shopping and residential streets.
